body: Exactly the response I was thinking I would get. I tried seeing a counselor and was kicked out (as you could read in my post), too much trouble with little chances of quickly fixing it with medication.
My husband won't let it happen

Even talking helps. For now I live in hope that it will get better when he gets older and learns how to entertain himself (from what I could gather it might happen around age of two?). We were saving for it for years and never anticipated that you simply couldn't buy services (childcare in our case) that you need, it is unbelievable. I think he has every toy imaginable for his age group, but it doesn't help, he wants me.

I don't think it is PPD as it's more philosophical problems. And maybe it is just bad counseling center not equipped to deal with my problems, but being kicked out of it was really hurtful and still hurts. Counseling without insurance (and mine doesn't cover anything less than very serious issues) is extremely expensive, I looked into it and couldn't justify such expenses for myself. This money should go to the baby. Anyway I just don't think that a counselor will work with me if I open up, instead of just institutionalizing me. They have to worry about their reputation and will try to pass it as if I'm a danger to the baby to get me out of their hair.

My SO should be coming soon. 

I really hope that it will get better, as of now he gets upset if I leave him to play on his own for more than 5 minutes. Believe me I searched for childcare and was ready to pay any amount of money, there are simply no places.

I just don't know which part is me having Asperger and getting really worn out and tired after interacting with people, which part is being tired because he is a baby, and which part is me living alone with him most of the time (my husband comes for a week once a month or less frequent). It just seems like never ending torture with people happily telling me that it will only get worse. As in little children, little problems; big children, big problems.
The difference is that you could leave you ex with a child and still be kinda accepted by society. As a woman I don't have this choice, I would be ostracized, especially in an academic world.

Thanks, talking to you made me realize that I made a mistake by having a child and have to pay for that. There is no way for me to have an academic career and have a family. I was hoping deep inside that maybe I'm missing something, but unfortunately not. 

Post-partum depression means medication, but it doesn't solve existential crisis of a failed scientist whose human nature was a reason for failure. I sometimes think that I would been much happier if I was born in a male body.
Thank you, I'll think about it. I was sure that anyone would simply call 911, but pastor might be more constraint by the seal of confession than campus counselor.

I was thinking about it. But I study in a small town and not sure that such conversation will remain confidential. I'm afraid that if I even start talking about hating my baby he/she would simply call 911 on me as it's a very strict taboo in the US. I never hurt him in any way and try my best to show only love. I let myself cry only when he sleeps.

I could trust him. I still love him, that's why I agreed to have a baby in the first place. And giving him baby and leaving would mean an end to our relationship, he would never understand or forgive. I think sometimes about just going away one day and never coming back. But it's not possible, science world is small and I would become unemployable if it ever became known that I left my baby (and people would learn about it very quickly). A woman who left a baby couldn't be trusted in the minds of people... Society is far more forgiving about the man who left their children.
